title: LIN-4254 piece 6: close-out-client onto loadWorld and remove close-out.js typeof seams (after LIN-4304)
description:
**Piece 6 of LIN-4254:** `close-out-client` **and the** `close-out.js` **seams. Last. Blocked by LIN-4304 (must be merged) and by Piece 5.**

## Slice of the approved plan

One PR, two commits:

1. **Production change:** remove the `typeof … === 'function'` seams in `public/close-out.js`. At `b581ac92` they are at `:159` (`typeof d.querySelector`), `:161` (`typeof main.getAttribute`), `:175` (`typeof d.querySelectorAll`) and `:187` (`typeof box.appendChild`). Re-read the lines once LIN-4304 lands. Also remove the entries for the first three from LIN-4304's allow-list. `:187` has no allow-list entry, because `appendChild` is outside LIN-4304's method list. It is removed anyway, since the boxes become real elements.
2. **Test move:** `tests/unit/close-out-client.test.js` (3 shapes: argument-seam boxes) onto `loadWorld`/`createFakeDom` + `parse`, with its private sandbox deleted and its census entry removed. `close-out-client:242` exists to feed those seams hand-made docs. Give it real markup and keep the test names by re-pointing them, not by deleting them.

## Outcome (close-out)

Implemented as approved in PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2331](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2331>) (merged as `ce42e721`): the four `typeof … === 'function'` seams are removed from `public/close-out.js`, `PRESENCE_ALLOW` is emptied, `close-out-client.test.js` runs on `loadWorld` with `renderCloseOutBox` markup (names unchanged), and its census entry is gone. One deviation, approved in review: `paint()` uses `replaceChildren` because the fake DOM does not model `firstChild`. The LIN-4304 gate (the reason this was a subtask rather than a step of LIN-4254) was discharged when LIN-4304 merged as `f742e5ac`. The full pre-prune description is in the task snapshots and the history is in the comment trail.

## Testing

* Common strategy, plus the sorted-name diff.
* A mutation per load-bearing assertion, against the real elements.
* Full unit suite green.

## Acceptance

* No `typeof … === 'function'` seams left in `close-out.js`, and their allow-list entries are gone.
* `close-out-client` is on `loadWorld` with its census entry removed.
* Names and counts are preserved.
* Census, line budget and full unit suite are green.

---

**Parent:** LIN-4254 (Move the 16 not-attempted client-test stubs onto the shared fake). This piece's starting point is the parent's approved **Implementation Plan** in LIN-4254's description, plus the builder notes in its approving Plan Review Verdict (comment `c1d9a66c-fb1a-4f25-903c-e11227c24ba7`). Follow it. Where the code shows it wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4254.

**Rules for every piece (from the plan):** "Moved" means the suite runs on `loadWorld` (`tests/unit/helpers/client-world.js` over `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`) and its private `vm.createContext` sandbox is deleted. Do not wrap the old sandbox around the fake. Slices and scripts that query the DOM at load use `loadWorld({ scripts: [] })`, then `parse(markup, document.body)`, then `world.run(source)`, as `observation-ruling-delivery` and LIN-4284 do. Router markup comes from the server's real renderer where one exists, not from hand-written HTML. Do not widen the fake. A file that hits an API the fake does not model (a `FakeDomError`, a `style` or layout read, or an unmodelled method such as `click()`) stays on `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES` with a `// stop:` comment naming the API and `file:line`. A `querySelector: () => null` stub that becomes a real tree can bring dead paths to life. A test that goes red there is a finding: classify it as a real client bug, a vacuous pass or a fake gap, and list it in the PR. Never loosen the test. Test names are kept. Do not split a file to keep a count, and do not copy a fixture.

**Testing strategy (every move PR):** an assertion map; before/after sorted test names, diffed against base; one mutation per load-bearing assertion, showing it goes red; and green runs of `fake-dom-census.test.js`, `claude-md-line-budget.test.js` and the full unit suite. The census count only falls. Every remaining entry's reason is true at merge.

**Grounding commits:** plan and approving review at `b581ac92` (Surveys at `b581ac926`); LIN-4292 landed as `b389f9b0`. Re-check `git log b581ac92..origin/main -- tests/unit public` before starting.

**Session fit:** fits one session
**Plan-review due:** no — covered by LIN-4254's approving plan-review (comment c1d9a66c-fb1a-4f25-903c-e11227c24ba7, rev 2)

comments.body: LIN-4304 has merged (`f742e5ac`) and deployed. This ticket is unblocked. The `close-out.js` allow-list entries in `tests/unit/public-element-method-guards.test.js` `PRESENCE_ALLOW` (the `typeof d.querySelector`, `typeof main.getAttribute` and `typeof d.querySelectorAll` seams) should be deleted in the same change that moves `close-out-client.test.js` onto the shared fake. The check's no-stale-entries test will fail until they are.

PR open: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2331 (branch feat/lin-4312-close-out-client-loadworld, commit 9b8771f0). Change: close-out-client.test.js onto loadWorld with the server renderer output; the close-out.js typeof seams removed; PRESENCE_ALLOW entries and the census entry deleted. Unit suite 23923/23923 locally. CI running; final summary follows once it completes.

LIN-4312 summary. PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2331 (commit 9b8771f0). CI green: CI success, Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan. Local: moved suite 18/18, neighbouring suites 182/182, full unit suite 23,923/23,923.

Changes: close-out.js typeof seams removed (pageAlreadyDone, pageHoldsDraft, noteReloadDeferred); paint() uses replaceChildren because the fake DOM does not model firstChild. close-out-client.test.js is on loadWorld with the server renderCloseOutBox output; test names unchanged. PRESENCE_ALLOW entries and the census entry deleted.

Evidence: the guard test fails on the original seams and passes on the change; 10 mutations each turn a moved test red.

Fake DOM gaps, reported and not widened: (1) firstChild reads undefined silently; session.js, live-console.js and ship.js use it, so their clear loops may be no-ops under test. (2) readOnly is not modelled; one test sets the property directly. Follow-up recommended.

Not merged. Merge is for review approval.

## Review — LIN-4312

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2331 at head `9b8771f0973d23883126932e9929a34e6087780b` (one commit on base `90542b2c` = current origin/main; MERGEABLE).

CI: green on head `9b8771f0`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan (source), CI success (run 42210566056).

### Scope vs plan
The diff touches 4 files: `public/close-out.js`, `tests/unit/close-out-client.test.js`, `tests/unit/fake-dom-census.test.js` and `tests/unit/public-element-method-guards.test.js`. It matches the ticket's slice:
- **Seams removed.** All four `typeof … === 'function'` seams are gone: the `:159`/`:161`/`:175` guards in `pageAlreadyDone`/`pageHoldsDraft`, and the `:187` `appendChild` guard in `noteReloadDeferred`.
- **Allow-list emptied.** `PRESENCE_ALLOW` is now `{}`.
- **Census.** The `close-out-client.test.js` entry is deleted.
- **Suite moved.** It runs on `loadWorld` with `renderCloseOutBox` server markup, and the private sandbox is gone.

**One deviation from the plan, and it is justified:** `paint()` now uses `replaceChildren` instead of the `firstChild` loop. That production change goes beyond the seam removal. It is recorded in the PR and in a code comment.

**Departure from the plan's wording:** it said "one PR, two commits", but this is a single commit. That is cosmetic and not blocking.

**Regression check.** `git log` on the 4 files since the ticket was created shows only the LIN-4254 sibling pieces and LIN-4304 (`f742e5ac`). No revert or fix is undone. LIN-4304's own allow-list comments said these entries were to be removed by this ticket.

### Independent checks (run by me at `9b8771f0`)
- **Suites green.** `close-out-client`, `public-element-method-guards`, `fake-dom-census` and `claude-md-line-budget`: 86/86 pass.
- **Test names unchanged.** I diffed the sorted spec-reporter names of `close-out-client.test.js` on base and on head: all 25 lines (suites and tests) are identical.
- **Mutations.** Each was made in `public/close-out.js` and reverted afterwards. Every one turns at least one test red:
  - **M1:** `pageAlreadyDone` ignores `data-status` → 2 fail
  - **M2:** `pageHoldsDraft` always false → 2 fail
  - **M3:** `paint` appends without clearing → 2 fail
  - **M4:** `paint` back on the old `firstChild` loop → 2 fail. This confirms the author's claim that the fake leaves stale children with that loop.
  - **M5:** `noteReloadDeferred` does nothing → 1 fail
  - **M6:** the `typeof d.querySelector` seam put back → the guard test fails
  - **M7:** the `!d` guard dropped → the no-document test fails
- **Full suite.** I did not re-run the full unit suite; CI's Unit tests job on this exact head is the gate.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
- **Seam class (inside):** handled completely. `PRESENCE_ALLOW` is empty, and the guard test proves no unlisted presence guard is left in `public/*.js`.
- **Fake-DOM gap class (outside):** the fake does not model `firstChild`, and reads it as `undefined` rather than throwing `FakeDomError`. It does not model `readOnly` either. This class is outside this ticket: it is a gap in `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`, not a close-out seam, and the plan says not to widen the fake here. Known siblings: `public/session.js:470` (`paintCloseOut`, the same clear loop as the old `paint`), `public/live-console.js:1381,1445` and `public/ship.js:1085`. Any `loadWorld` test that goes through these may pass vacuously. Close-out should file one follow-up, after checking none exists (I found none):
  - make the fake model `firstChild`/`readOnly`, or throw `FakeDomError` on them;
  - then re-check the suites that reach those lines.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **`paint()` under `replaceChildren` in a real browser — inside** (this ticket's own production change). No e2e drives a client-side repaint through `close-out.js`. `tests/e2e/close-out.spec.js:204` asserts `run-evidence-closeout-neutral` on the session page. That line can come from the server render or from `session.js`'s own `paintCloseOut`, not from `close-out.js` `paint()`. Risk is low: `replaceChildren` is standard DOM and already used in `public/app.js:765` and `public/chart-helpers.js`.
  - **Settle before the merge:** open a task page with a stop-at-PR close-out box in `data-state="ready"`, and in the browser console run `CloseOut.applyCloseOutState(box, {status:'merged', message:'x'})`. Right: the box has exactly one child, `p[data-testid=run-evidence-closeout-neutral]`. Wrong: the earlier children remain.
  - **Rollback:** revert `9b8771f0` (squash commit on main).
- **The `readOnly` branch of `pageHoldsDraft` — inside** (a claim the moved test depends on). The test sets `fields[i].readOnly = true` by hand, because the fake does not reflect the `readonly` attribute. So the test proves the branch, not the attribute-to-property link. That link is standard browser behaviour, and the production code is unchanged there.
  - **Settle before the merge:** the browser check above covers this too. On a task page whose share box has `readonly` and text, `CloseOut.pageHoldsDraft()` returns false. It returns true once you type in a writable text field.
- **Fake-DOM `firstChild`/`readOnly` gaps in sibling suites — outside.** Close-out files the follow-up described above. This deliverable's correctness does not depend on it.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The work is complete against the acceptance criteria: seams and allow-list gone, census entry removed, names identical, and every load-bearing assertion is mutation-proven. CI is green on `9b8771f0`. What remains is one quick in-browser check of `paint()`/`pageHoldsDraft`, plus filing the outside fake-gap follow-up.

## Close-out — LIN-4312

**Merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2331, squash-merged as `ce42e7217beb6498c347342ec97be1af109c6151`, pinned with `--match-head-commit 9b8771f0973d23883126932e9929a34e6087780b`, the head the review approved and CI passed on. Review verdict on record: Approve, conditional on the ledger below.

**Changes I made after approval:** none. No review fix needed code, so the head merged is the head reviewed.

**CI:** CI applies (`.github/workflows/test.yml`). Fresh read before the merge: CI success, Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4 and Secret scan (source) all pass on `9b8771f0` (run 42210566056); PR was MERGEABLE/CLEAN. After the merge, the `Tests` run on main at `ce42e721` completed with success.

**Deploy:** the live footer at harbour.cat showed `90542b2c` after the merge and `ce42e721` once it landed. I fetched the served `close-out.js` and it is byte-identical to `public/close-out.js` on merged main: 0 `typeof … === 'function'` seams, `replaceChildren` present.

### Ledger
* **`paint()` under `replaceChildren` in a real browser (inside): settled before the merge.** I ran the PR head's `public/close-out.js` and `renderCloseOutBox` markup (a stop-at-PR box in `data-state="ready"`) in headless Chromium and called `CloseOut.applyCloseOutState(box, {status:'merged', message:'x'})`. Before: 3 element children. After: exactly 1 child, `p[data-testid=run-evidence-closeout-neutral]` with text `x`, `data-state="merged"`, no stale children. A second repaint to `closed` also left exactly 1 child (`run-evidence-closeout-setup`). No page or console errors. Caveat: this was a minimal page built from the real renderer's output, not a full task page.
* **`readOnly` branch of `pageHoldsDraft` (inside): settled before the merge, same session.** In Chromium a parsed `<input type="text" readonly value="…">` reads `readOnly === true` (attribute reflected). `pageHoldsDraft()` returned false with only the read-only field holding text, true once a writable textarea held text, and true for the same field once `readOnly` was set false. `pageAlreadyDone()` returned false on `data-status="in-progress"` and true on `done`.
* **Fake-DOM `firstChild` / `readOnly` gaps in sibling suites (outside): follow-ups.** Existing ticket LIN-4291 already names the `firstChild` gap (searched; it was Backlog, Low). I added a comment there with the new anchors review found (`public/session.js:470`, `public/ship.js:1085`; `live-console.js` was already listed) and did not file a duplicate. The `readOnly` gap was not covered anywhere, so I filed **LIN-4329** (Low, labels `Improvement` + `kind:follow-up`, related to LIN-4291), written to stand alone, with problem, why it matters, acceptance, anchors and an "Unvalidated idea".
* **Named monitor / rollback:** review's rollback is to revert `9b8771f0` (the squash commit on main, `ce42e721`). No monitor was named, and I did not supply one.

**Not run:** the full unit suite on my side. CI's Unit tests job on the exact head and on main at `ce42e721` is the gate, as review said.

**Housekeeping:** description archived before pruning (snapshot captured 2026-11-06T11:40:34Z, checked against the pre-prune description) and then pruned: the LIN-4304 gating rationale is replaced by an outcome stub. Problem, scope, testing, acceptance and the session-fit and plan-review lines are untouched. Blocker LIN-4304 and sibling pieces 2–5 are already Done. The parent LIN-4254 is handled below.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was it difficult?** Moderately, and not where expected. The seams and allow-list deletions were mechanical. The change got stuck on the fake DOM's *silent* gaps: `firstChild` and `readOnly` read as `undefined` instead of throwing. So `paint()`'s `while (box.firstChild)` loop did nothing, and only a count assertion caught it (`children.length` 4, not 1). The rules didn't fit. "Don't widen the fake" plus "an unmodelled API means a stop on the census" assume a stopped file keeps its hand-written fake. But removing the seams breaks the old sandbox (its doc had no `querySelector`), so a stop meant not landing. My workaround: `paint()` now uses `replaceChildren` (equivalent, used 8 times in `public/`), and one test sets `readOnly` itself. Both were judgment calls, and the first changed production for a test's sake.

**2. What first?** Check every DOM member `close-out.js` reads against what `fake-dom.js` models. Ten minutes, and both gaps would have shown up before any test went red.

**3. What would I tidy?** Make the fake throw on unmodelled property reads, so a silent `undefined` becomes a `FakeDomError` and the stop rule applies. Then model `firstChild` (`session.js`, `live-console.js` and `ship.js` read it too) and `readOnly`, and drop my shim and `paint()`'s fake-specific comment. The census also needs a way to say "moved, but hit a gap".

**4. The ideal ticket:** "Delete close-out.js's unit-seam guards." One commit: the suite already on a fake that fails loudly, and the allow-list shrinking as a side effect.

**5. What the ticket got wrong:** It assumed the fake was complete enough here, and that a gap would always show up as a thrown error. Its line references were accurate. It asked for two commits; I made one, because the seam removal and the test move only pass together.

**6. What it left behind:** `PRESENCE_ALLOW` is now empty: the mechanism stays, with no entries. `paint()` explains itself in terms of a test helper, so that knowledge lives in two places. The `firstChild` gap is recorded only in PR #2331 and on this ticket. Neither `fake-dom.js`'s header nor the three other scripts' suites know about it, and those suites may be passing without anything being cleared. Simpler: `close-out.js` lost four guards, and the suite lost its private sandbox. The suite renders boxes with `renderCloseOutBox`, so renderer drift now breaks the client test, as it should.

**7. Did the larger scope pay?** I don't know what the Survey recommended, so I can only judge the scope I had. Coupling the seam removal to the test move paid for itself: the two can't be split, because removing the seams breaks the old sandbox and the stale-entry check forces the allow-list deletions into the same change. The cost was that rules written for the whole move were applied to the one piece where they conflicted. I'd keep the content, but let a piece model one missing fake member, with its own test in `fake-dom.test.js`, rather than forbidding widening outright.
